questions.q: What did John F. Kennedy do before deciding how to respond to Soviet missiles in Cuba?
a: He paused to reflect, swimming and spending time in the Rose Garden
He gathered his advisors for an immediate vote on an attack
He ordered the missile sites destroyed without further delay
He flew to Moscow to negotiate with Soviet leaders in person
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes Kennedy writing notes, swimming in the White House pool and sitting in the Rose Garden before choosing a response.

questions.q: Which response did Kennedy ultimately choose in the Cuban Missile Crisis?
a: A blockade that gave his opponent time to think as well
An immediate air strike on the missile sites
A trade of American missiles for Soviet ones
A complaint filed with the United Nations
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Kennedy settled on a blockade of Cuba, which let Kruschev reflect before writing back.

questions.q: According to lesson 2, what does letting silence into your life allow you to do?
a: Notice things you would otherwise miss
Escape from other people completely
Think faster when under pressure
Avoid conversations you find difficult
questions.why: Lesson 2 says quietness lets us pick up on ideas and feelings that noise would drown out.

questions.q: What is unusual about John Cage's musical piece 4'33?
a: It consists of pure silence lasting four minutes and 33 seconds
It is performed on four pianos at the same time
It repeats a single note 433 times without pause
It must always be played outdoors in bad weather
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes Cage's best-known work as a piece made entirely of silence.

questions.q: What did Anders Ericsson's study of violinists find about the best performers?
a: They slept more and napped more than the others
They practiced far longer hours than the others
They began training later than the others
They played more concerts than the others
questions.why: Lesson 3 notes that the strongest violinists got more sleep and napped more often than their peers.
